verdictScope: m1-successor-subject-02 only: the developer design-lock v2 unit (design-lock.json schemaVersion 2, tools/verify_design.py, tools/tests/test_design_binding.py). Not full M1, product qualification or release approval. The concurrent metadata-v1 architecture work is not reviewed.
reviewKind: nonblind correction review of SUCC-R1-01 (continuation of m1-successor-review-01)

closedFindings.evidence: The only subject change is additive: rebound(), refuse_with() and four isolated tests in InventorySuccessorTests (tools/tests/test_design_binding.py:225-276); the eight existing successor tests are unchanged. rebound() now copies full pins, adding bytes to review.successorRecord and assent.actualClaudeReview, which the verifier ignores as extra fields. The parent-selection fixture restores the original base inputs, so only the selected-input guard can refuse. 21 tests pass. The unchanged 26-mutant probe kills 25 on the live tests; the sole survivor is M02, shown equivalent in review-01 (the pin digest and zero-addition checks cover it). Before the correction, 14 mutants survived. The protection is redundant: with rebinding removed, or with regex assertions downgraded to a generic DesignError, the kill set is the same. With both removed, 17 of 35 survive (probes/mutants-no-rebind-no-regex.log), which shows the probe is sensitive.

carriedForwardAdvisories.status: unchanged, nonblocking, not claimed fixed. The verifier bytes are identical to subject01, so the SUCC-A1-01 Python-equality behaviour still applies; the reviewed real rows are strictly JSON-equal.

newAdvisories.title: Finer strictness of successor guards is not pinned by tests
newAdvisories.evidence: Nine new mutants (N27-N35) were added. Six survive the 21 tests: N28/N29 (review and record parent joins ignore bytes), N30 (truthy rootSubstantiveAssent), N31 (missing or falsy review requiredFindings tolerated), N32 (truthy record preservation flag) and N34 (parent selected by path only). N34 is equivalent: a parent pin sharing an input path but with a different sha or bytes is refused by pin digest/length checks on the real lock (probes/n34_equivalence.log). N28/N29 leave content still bound by SHA-256, so they could only admit inconsistent size metadata. N30-N32 are real strictness regressions the tests would miss. The identical verifier refuses these inputs today (review-01 adversarial probes: rootSubstantiveAssent 1, parentArtifactBytesUnchanged "true" and missing requiredFindings are all refused). Optional: add three one-line isolated cases.
